## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

While no external canonical parallels are established, computational analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse, identifying 51 matching passages shared across 11 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. In particular, nearly the entire early portion of the text (§0.3–8.4) is reflected in the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (Paṭhamo bhāgo), with 25 matching passages amounting to over 2,700 shared characters, as well as additional matches in the second part of the commentary [DharmaNexus]. Standard apadāna verses—especially within the terminal passage §8.3/9.3–13.1—are shared with multiple other poems in the Therāpadāna, such as the *Padumapūjakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 132), *Tivaṇṭipupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 192), *Kāsumāriphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 382), *Maṇipūjakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 180), and *Citakapūjakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 118) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns low-scoring text matches with the Tibetan *Vinayavastu* (D0001-2), representing non-parallel phraseological commonalities [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
